scope: Pinned CP8.3.2 bootstrap identities and actual retained records on three wholly disposable Compose volumes; Kubernetes exact-byte ConfigMap rendering only at this checkpoint.

runtime_inventory.bootstrap_language: Python3.9.25 stdlib already bundled in pinned broker image; no hub dependency/image/service added
runtime_inventory.broker_license: Apache Kafka core Apache-2.0, bundled components retain their own licenses
runtime_inventory.proxy_license: Confluent Community License baseline; no security plugin needed for this identity probe

tested_cases: Two independent fresh default installations generated distinct real broker cluster IDs.
Fresh Docker volume permissions allow provisioning as the selected broker user before upstream initialization.
Seeds private, exclusive and synced before upstream storage formatting; restart preserved each cluster ID.
A third fresh fixture first used the original upstream startup and old tutorial cluster ID, then the new bootstrap adopted its existing metadata.
Real topic record and offset0 retained across restart/adoption on all three volumes.
Wrong explicit cluster ID rejected before upstream formatting, with explicit mismatch error.
Local checks reject seed/meta/node disagreement, symlinks, path traversal, unidentified data and duplicate metadata.
Kubernetes ConfigMap exactly mirrors source and removes shared constant ID.
All owned containers, networks and volumes removed; no existing service changed.
limits: Single-node identity/service proof; not an app lifecycle, backup/restore or production HA qualification.
Kubernetes fsGroup/runtime proof remains separate until executed on the exact final deployment.
Bootstrap lock fences seed provisioning only; one broker owns the volume and Kafka retains log-directory locking.
